habit_scope: Devices, fixtures, grilles, and equipment after interior finish and paint. Leftover of CMHC Ch19/20 after rough. Hold points, not a how-to.
how_it_is_done: CMHC Ch2 Paint, Cabinets and Fixtures: painting first, then ceramic backsplashes, then electrical receptacles, light fixtures and smoke alarms and equipment such as furnaces, water heaters, mechanical ventilation, stoves and clothes dryers. Heating contractor installs grilles/registers (forced air) or radiators (hydronic/electric baseboard). Ensure installations have been inspected and function; operating instructions and warranties provided. Final clean-up. About two weeks.

Ch19: Connect plumbing fixtures and accessories after interior finish. Lighting fixtures, switches, outlets and cover plates after interior finish and painting. Smoke alarms: hard-wired, no disconnect between alarm and panel, not on a wall-outlet circuit; in or near each bedroom on each storey including basements; certified (ULC named — Canadian). Interconnection not required unless a secondary suite. 2-story three-ways already roughed (P12). CO detectors for bedrooms adjacent to garages (Ch27) — Canadian, confirm AHJ. Do not invent GFCI lists. Device-height trim SOP: Gap. Ch19 typical switch ~1.4 m (4 ft 6 in) is the rough/planning sentence, not a P16 fastener schedule.

Ch20 leftover: equipment access space; ducts outside the envelope sealed and insulated to wall level; exhaust openings with damper. Appliances strapped/braced where earthquake or local rules require — confirm AHJ. Keep drywall dust out of ducts was a rough-stage insight — do not load dust at trim either. Equipment set after paint, not at P12 rough.
Pre-occupancy / final plumbing, heating and electrical inspection (Ch2 Fig 2). Completion Inspection (Interior and Exterior) after that. No skip-inspection.

when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Setting devices before paint. Skipping final MEP inspection. Inventing IRC smoke-alarm section numbers.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They trim out. What they skip is paint-before-devices and the final MEP inspection.

risk_if_swapped_late: Changing furnace type after the flue/combustion opening is in is a framing patch. Catch at rough.
plain_language_summary: Paint first. Then plugs, lights, toilets, furnace, grilles. Hard-wired smoke alarms by the bedrooms. Inspector looks. No skip-inspection. Hand over the manuals.
